newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to launch debt trading system.
newsitem.headline: Russia to launch debt trading system.

text.p: Russia's Federal Securities Commission is setting up a system for paperless trading of debt of Russian companies, banks and municipalities, commission chairman Dmitry Vasilyev said on Tuesday.
The Promissory Note Information System will quote prices for veksel promissory notes, he told a news conference.
Veksel notes are issued on the basis of companies' and municipalities' debts and are a way of making them tradable.
Vasilyev said trading was due to start in one to two weeks, with Commission financing the work of the system during the first two months.
Because many institutions in Russia are behind in paying their bills and the whole economy is crippled by a non-payments crisis, the market is potentially huge, and worth trillions of roubles.
Veksel notes are already traded actively in documentary form in Russia, but the market is extremely risky and several frauds have been perpetrated.
Vasilyev said the commission would strictly control the new system to prevent such frauds.

Operators from Russia and other former Soviet republics would be able to quote daily prices and possible bids and offers of non-documentary notes via electronic mail to the commission, which will act as system administrator, he said.
The administrator would then send the summarised information to all operators.
